title: The Promise of Sandpiper Point Anew
premise: Felix Ashgrove has spent ten years curating other people's love stories in his bookshop at Sandpiper Point while refusing his own, ever since the night his fiancée, Marisol, left town with his best friend Theo. When a freak snowstorm strands all three of them — along with Felix's sharp-eyed daughter, who has secretly invited both guests to her father's birthday — old letters and a hidden deed reveal that Marisol left not from betrayal but because she was protecting Felix from a debt tied to his inheritance. As the ferry deadline looms, Felix must choose between the comfortable lie he's built his life on and the truth that could restore everything. They say the rehearsed sentence — 'I choose you, again, on purpose' — just as the last ferry sounds its horn, and this time no one boards it.
about_author: Beatrix Okafor is a former coastal librarian who writes second-chance romances set in small towns where everyone knows everyone's business. She lives a ferry ride from the mainland with her partner and an unreasonable number of annotated paperbacks.

chapters.title: The Guest List Nobody Wrote
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Preparing the bookshop for his daughter Nell's surprise-planned birthday gathering, Felix discovers she has invited both Marisol and Theo — the two people he's avoided for a decade. The chapter establishes his guarded tenderness and the town's gossip mill. Emotional beat: dread laced with longing, as Felix realizes his daughter has been quietly investigating the past he buried.

chapters.title: Snowfall Between Old Pages
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Felix and Marisol. The storm hits early; roads close, ferries suspend, and the four of them are trapped overnight in the bookshop's upper flat. A spilled box of unsold romance novels becomes an accidental confessional game, and Marisol's deflections crack. Emotional beat: warmth rekindling against both their wills, while Theo watches the distance between them shrink.

chapters.title: The Deed in the Dust Jacket
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Nell finds a property deed hidden inside a hollowed-out first edition: the bookshop was nearly lost to debt ten years ago, and Marisol secretly paid it off before leaving, believing Felix would refuse help out of pride. Confronted, Felix's decade of resentment collapses into shame and fury. Emotional beat: the climax — truth detonating loyalty, with Theo finally confessing his own role in the silence.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Morning breaks clear; the final ferry of the season departs at noon, and Marisol is packed to leave for good. At the dock, with Nell and Theo as reluctant witnesses, Felix says the sentence they've each rehearsed for ten years — 'I choose you, again, on purpose' — and asks her to stay not out of debt but desire. Emotional beat: resolution and release; she misses the ferry deliberately, and the family walks home together.
